eval_dimensions.name: Notification Transport Resolution
eval_dimensions.description: Step 3 resolves Slack vs Google Chat from whichever per-repo config names the repo, runs both when both do, and asks when neither does (GH-1308)

eval_dimensions.name: Approval State Precheck
eval_dimensions.description: Step 1.5 filters bot approvals before matching reviews against headRefOid, and gates on a human approval of the current HEAD

eval_dimensions.name: Skill Delegation
eval_dimensions.description: Assignment and notification are delegated to the sibling skills, never inlined as raw gh or API calls

evals.name: chat-only-repo-reaches-its-transport
evals.description: GH-1308: the repo is named only in the Google Chat config. Before the fix, Step 3 was hardcoded to Slack and a Chat-only team had no supported path through this skill — the observed session passed the transport as a free-text argument and the agent substituted the sibling skill on its own.

assertions.text: Delegates to Dev10x:gchat-review-request, the transport whose config names the repo
Does NOT invoke the Slack sibling — its config does not name this repo
Step 4 summary reports Google Chat rather than a hardcoded 'Slack notification' line

evals.name: both-configs-name-the-repo
evals.description: Mirroring review requests into Slack and Chat is a legitimate configuration, so Step 3 must not assume exactly one transport.

assertions.text: Invokes both sibling skills rather than picking one

evals.name: no-config-fires-the-transport-gate
evals.description: Neither config names the repo. The skill must ask where the request should go rather than failing into silence or guessing a transport.

assertions.text: Fires AskUserQuestion — a plain-text question would let the skill auto-proceed without an answer
The widget offers Slack, Google Chat, and Skip the notification
Neither sibling skill is invoked before the user answers

evals.name: bot-approval-does-not-short-circuit
evals.description: GH-128: only a bot has approved the current HEAD. A bot approval must not satisfy the human-review requirement, so the skill proceeds to request review rather than offering to merge.

assertions.text: Continues to Step 2 instead of firing the skip-and-merge gate

evals.name: human-approval-on-head-fires-the-merge-gate
evals.description: A human has approved the current HEAD, so pinging reviewers again is noise. The skill must ask rather than silently short-circuiting.

assertions.text: Fires AskUserQuestion with Skip / Force request / Cancel

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the request-review skill

should_trigger.query: this PR is ready, ping the team and assign reviewers
should_trigger.rationale: Wants both GitHub assignment and a chat notification — the combined entry point

should_trigger.query: request review on #42 and let the team know in chat
should_trigger.rationale: Explicitly names both halves of this skill's job

should_not_trigger.query: assign @alice as reviewer, no notification needed
should_not_trigger.rationale: GitHub assignment only — use Dev10x:gh-pr-request-review directly

should_not_trigger.query: post a message to the team channel about the outage
should_not_trigger.rationale: General chat post, unrelated to a review request — use Dev10x:slack or Dev10x:gchat

should_not_trigger.query: the PR is still a draft, hold off
